question: Which of the following industrial sectors were prioritized during the Second Five-Year Plan?

options.text: Iron and steel industry, fertilizer industry, heavy engineering, and lignite projects

solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron and steel industry, fertilizer industry, heavy engineering, and lignite projects**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan of India** (1956–61) focused on the development of heavy industries, which were crucial for building a strong industrial base in the nation.
 
• The plan emphasized sectors such as the **iron and steel industry**, as they were foundational for infrastructure and industrial development.
 
• The **fertilizer industry** was prioritized to improve agricultural productivity and support India's growing population.
 
• **Heavy engineering projects** were undertaken to develop machinery and equipment needed for industrial production.
 
• **Lignite projects** were included to diversify energy resources and reduce dependence on imported energy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61):**

 
 
• It was guided by the **socialist model of development**, inspired by the Soviet Union.
 
• The plan was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, which prioritized heavy industries over consumer goods production.
 
• Its objective was to achieve **self-reliance and economic stability** by developing a strong industrial base.
 
 
 
• **Iron and Steel Industry:**
 
 
• The establishment of major steel plants such as **Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur** became a hallmark of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
• It laid the foundation for modern industrial infrastructure in India.
 
 
 
• **Fertilizer Industry:**
 
 
• Key focus on producing chemical fertilizers to enhance **agricultural productivity**.
 
• Helped address India's food security challenges during the post-independence era.
 
 
 
• **Heavy Engineering:**
 
 
• Industries like machinery manufacturing and equipment production were strengthened.
 
• These industries supported other sectors such as power, transportation, and agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Lignite Projects:**
 
 
• Lignite, a type of coal, was developed as an alternative energy resource.
 
• Such projects reduced dependence on imported coal and diversified India's energy portfolio.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Model:**

 
 
• Developed by statistician **P.C. Mahalanobis**, the model emphasized the role of the industrial sector in economic growth.
 
• It allocated significant resources to heavy industries and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Second Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• It led to the establishment of India's industrial base and created job opportunities in various sectors.
 
• Although successful in industrial development, the plan faced criticism for neglecting the **agriculture sector**, which caused food shortages.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• The focus on heavy industries led to **imbalances** in resource allocation.
 
• India faced a **foreign exchange crisis** as imports rose and exports stagnated during this period.
